slides.h: A new study opens: the anti-Copernican discriminant
b: The reading found the gap — the interior branch violates the Copernican principle in print, and nobody ever computed the consequence.
Phase 4 manufactures the branch's first calibrated test. Brief frozen on your go, sha-pinned.

slides.h: Off-center inside a horizon → the sky is not the same in every direction
b: Derive the observables from the exact solutions: an H₀ dipole, a non-kinematic CMB excess, horizon-scale suppression.
Either the data bounds the offset — the branch's first calibrated statement — or the observable-scale branch dies. Both count.
The FRW interior is exactly homogeneous — so all anisotropy must enter through the direction-dependent distance to the shock.
Prove it or refute it first. Kill criteria named in the brief: untestable, below-sensitivity, and no new dials without a gate.
